title: Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Chief (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC PP&O
raw_text:
4. MOS 5769, Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Defense
Chief (MGySgt to SSgt) PMOS, DC PP&O

    a. Summary. The CBRN Defense Chief serves as a CBRN defense SME to
advise the staff and coordinate CBRN defense, reconnaissance, and
decontamination operations. CBRN Defense Chiefs plan, coordinate and monitor
the employment of unit CBRN defense, reconnaissance, and decontamination
equipment, and attached capabilities, and serve in the unit combat operations
center to perform CBRN warning and reporting, and coordinate CBRN response
activities. In addition to advising the Commander on the operational and
technical functions associated with CBRN defense, CBRN reconnaissance, CBRN
response, and CBRN decontamination, senior-level management Marines (MGySgt
to MSgt) also advise the commander and staff on events related to supporting
countering weapons of mass destruction (CWMD) in support of combatant command
lines of effort and objectives within the supported area of operations. CBRN



                                        3-326                          Enclosure (1)
 3135                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



Defense Chiefs at MSC and higher or joint commands are responsible to assist
the CBRN Defense Officer with integrating the execution of CWMD in plans,
exercises, and operations through organization, training, and planning. They
support operations across the spectrum of special operations as fully
integrated special staff members in a variety of special operations forces or
joint task organized configurations.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess PMOS 5711.

            (2) Attain promotion to SSgt.

            (3) Security requirement:

            (a) Active adjudicated secret clearance prior to attendance of
the USMC CBRN Defense Chief Course, Ft Leonard Wood, MO.

            (b) For MSgt/MGySgt: must meet sensitive compartmented
information (SCI) eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background
investigation (SSBI)/tier 5 (T5) investigation. This is required in
performance of duties associated with MARFOR to MSC and joint billet(s).

    c. Requirements. CBRN Defense Specialists MOS 5713 terminates at staff
sergeant. As such, completion of the CBRN Defense Chiefs Course (A16KJK4) at
Ft Leonard Wood, MO is required within two years after selection to the grade
of staff sergeant (completion as a sergeant of two year of more in grade is
authorized). Any staff sergeant who has not completed the CBRN Defense
Chiefs Course after two years will be deemed unqualified and subject to
Enlisted Career Force Controls (ECFC), in alignment with expected career
progression standards. Promotion to gunnery sergeant, master sergeant, or
master gunnery sergeant is not permissible in the absence of the PMOS 5769
skill certification. Exception: sergeants selected for promotion to staff
sergeant while assigned to a special duty assignment (SDA) will have their
two-year course completion window start upon execution of orders to a new
unit following the conclusion of their SDA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks refer to
reference (ap), Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense
Training and Readiness Manual and MOS road map.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

        (1) Mid-level Management Marines (GySgt to SSgt) holding mid-level
management ranks perform the related duties from the entry level ranks with
the following additional classifications:

                (a) Emergency Management Specialists 13-1061.

                (b) Occupational Health and Safety Specialists 29-9011.

            (c) First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Officer and Administrative
Support Workers 43-1011.

        (2) Senior-level Management Marines (MGySgt to MSgt) holding senior
level management billets (MARFOR to MSC) perform the related duties from the
previous classifications with the following classifications:



                                          3-327                      Enclosure (1)
 3135                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



                (a) Management Analyst 13/14-1111.

                (b) General and Operations Managers 11-1021.

                (c) Command and Control Center Specialists 55-3015.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Advisor, 0570.

            (2) Operational Advisor, 0571.




                                        3-328                          Enclosure (1)
 3136                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: (CBRN) DEFENSE 1. Introduction. The Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear (CBRN) Defense Occupational Field includes planning and employing capabilities to enable the organization to accomplish its mission in a CBRN environment. This consists of forces capable of planning, detecting, identifying, warning and reporting, and mitigation of CBRN threats and hazards. CBRN Defense Specialists advise the staff on chemical and biological (CB) warfare agent characteristics, physiological symptoms and effects, treatment, detection and identification. They must coordinate and conduct training to ensure the organization is capable of mitigating the effects of nuclear explosions and detection of radiological hazards. CBRN Defense Specialist effectively instruct CBRN defense individual and unit survival measures and provide more in-depth training to their unit's CBRN defense team members. Additionally, CBRN Defense Specialists must be familiar with the proper employment, operation, maintenance, and supply procedures for all CBRN defense equipment and materials down to the battalion/squadron level.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
